clue.text: For example, fine part of a football match

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fine is one kind of punishment imposed for breaking a rule
second meaning: the spot kick awarded after a foul in the box

explanation.surface: Someone describing a fine passage of play during a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' turns 'fine' from a compliment into an instance of a wider category, so the first definition names the category, not the fine itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A monetary fine is one sort of punishment; in football the word also names the free shot at goal from twelve yards.

clue.text: Son put in school on road heading north in EU state

indicators.note: to put something in something else places one piece inside another

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
S is the standard abbreviation for son

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A boy enrolled at a school in some European country, travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite English boarding school; the A1 runs from London to Edinburgh, and the digit 1 stands in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic republic joined the European Union in 2004, so it is one of the bloc's member countries.

clue.text: Check German car close to roundabout

parts.note: Audi is a German car manufacturer

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it ends, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Inspecting a German car that has pulled up near a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads like a command to look at the car, but it is the definition; 'close to' means the last letter, not 'near'.
explanation.definitionFit: To audit accounts is to inspect or examine them officially, so the verb works as a synonym for verify.

clue.text: Framework for plants still in a wild state around middle of area

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so one piece surrounds another
something wild is untamed and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central portion, so only the centre letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of this four-letter word

explanation.surface: Garden plants that are still growing wild around the middle of some patch of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb about the plants, but it is raw material to be scrambled, with the centre of 'area' placed inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice of wood or wire fixed to a wall so that climbing plants can grow up it.

clue.text: Directors need these self-catering trips sorted out

indicators.note: sorting things out rearranges them, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: SC is a standard abbreviation for self-catering in holiday listings
taken as written

explanation.surface: Company directors need their self-catering business trips organised properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directors' suggests a boardroom, but the definition means film or stage directors; SC is the abbreviation seen in holiday cottage adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Film and theatre directors work from the written text of a play or screenplay, which is what they must have.

clue.text: Poor introduction to complicated card game

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
rummy is a card game of collecting sets and runs

explanation.surface: A disappointing explanation of how to play a complicated card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor introduction' reads as one phrase about a bad explanation; the definition is 'Poor' on its own and 'introduction to' picks a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy or of low quality, so it matches the adjective meaning inferior.

clue.text: Alteration of invites to incorporate two points is very thorough

indicators.note: to incorporate something is to take it inside, so one piece holds another
an alteration changes a thing's form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
E and N are compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Changing an invitation list to include a couple of extra points makes it very comprehensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' in crosswords are usually compass directions; here two of them sit inside the rearranged INVITES.
explanation.definitionFit: An intensive course or search is concentrated and exhaustive, covering everything in depth, hence very thorough.

clue.text: Feature of a pig getting to move unsteadily? About right

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to totter is to walk shakily
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pig staggering about, and the question of which part of it makes it wobble.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: the part before it asks about the pig's body, and 'About right' is the instruction to wrap TOTTER around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A trotter is a pig's foot, a body part and a butcher's cut, so it is one physical characteristic of the animal.

clue.text: Man encroaches in order to undertake something risky

indicators.note: putting things in order sorts them afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A man trespasses on purpose so as to attempt something dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order to' reads as a single purpose phrase, but it splits into the rearrangement signal and a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance your arm is a British idiom for taking a gamble or trying something with a real possibility of failing.

clue.text: Boss in horse breeding establishment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised knob or ornamental projection on a surface, as on a shield
second meaning: a farm where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.surface: The manager in charge at a horse breeding farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' pretends to mean a manager; its other sense is a projecting knob, as on a shield or ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative raised knob can be called either word, and the same word names a farm keeping stallions and mares for breeding.

clue.text: First person at work behind outlet for motor vehicles showing fatigue

indicators.note: what is behind comes after, so these pieces follow the other one in the answer

parts.note: the pipe through which a car's engine fumes escape
the first person singular pronoun
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: The first person clocking on at a car showroom looking worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' suggests the earliest arrival, but it is the grammatical first person; 'outlet' sounds like a shop selling cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaustion is a state of extreme tiredness, so it is a stronger synonym for weariness.

clue.text: Gradually add joins, tiling? Not altogether!

indicators.note: not taking the words altogether means using only part of them, so the letters sit inside

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A tiler gradually filling in the joints, but not doing the whole job at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'joINS TILing', ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea or quality is to introduce it little by little, drop by drop, into someone's mind.

clue.text: Put forward minister, one entertained by celebrity

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within the host's home, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: note means fame or distinction, as in 'a person of note'
MIN is the abbreviation for minister
a means one

explanation.surface: Proposing a government minister who has been hosted by a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrity' is the abstract quality, fame, not a famous person, which is why it gives NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate a candidate is to propose them formally for election or office, which is to put their name forward.

clue.text: Obstacle covering street for legal professional

indicators.note: a covering lies over and around something, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a barrier is something that blocks the way
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A roadblock across the street getting in the way of a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: In England a barrister is the kind of lawyer who argues cases in court, as distinct from a solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer qualified to plead in the higher courts, so the title names one kind of legal practitioner.

clue.text: Note mix of cards for change of politicians?

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
mixing a pack of cards before dealing

explanation.surface: A short memo about shuffling a deck, as if a card game explained a political change.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a playful description: a cabinet change is a card shuffle of ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet reshuffle is when a prime minister moves ministers between posts, rearranging the government's senior team.

clue.text: Piece of dishonesty about dietary material

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone telling a lie about what they have been eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a joining word but supplies RE, the Latin-derived 'concerning' seen in letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary fibre, also called roughage, is the indigestible plant matter in food that aids digestion.

clue.text: Fellow left to request container for liquids

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
L is the abbreviation for left
to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A man left behind to ask for something to carry drinks in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as a verb, departed, but it is the direction abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A flask is a narrow-necked bottle or vacuum vessel used for carrying drinks or holding chemicals.

clue.text: New idol after playing requires short sleep

indicators.note: the letters are presented as they end up after being played about with, so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A new pop star needs a nap after performing a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'after playing' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-down is a brief rest on a bed or sofa, often with a nap, much like a quick doze.

clue.text: In turn, refer to Green when mobilised being full of vitality?

indicators.note: mobilising troops moves them about, so the letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to cite a source is to refer to it

explanation.surface: Environmental activists, the Greens, getting lively once they are organised into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' sounds like 'one after another', but it reverses CITE; the capital G on Green is just surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone energetic has plenty of vigour and liveliness, which is what having lots of vitality means.

clue.text: Break to tour very large island? That's extremely optimistic

indicators.note: a tour goes all the way round a place, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a rest is a break from work
OS stands for outsize, the clothing label for very large
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A holiday touring a huge island, which is as hopeful as a plan can be.
explanation.walkthrough: OS for outsize appears on British clothing labels; the definition is superlative, matching 'extremely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosy outlook is a hopeful, cheerful one, and the superlative form means the most hopeful possible.

clue.text: This person's quietly over for treatment to get better

parts.note: 'this person is' from the setter's view is 'I am', contracted

indicators.note: something given treatment is worked on and altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A patient quietly going in for medical treatment in the hope of recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter speaking of themselves, so 'this person's' is I'M; the medical surface makes 'treatment' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve is to become healthier or of higher quality, the everyday sense of recovering or making progress.

clue.text: Niche in a large seaside bay

parts.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a cove is a small sheltered bay on the coast

explanation.surface: A sheltered nook within a broad bay along the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but only links definition to wordplay; the pieces simply run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess set back into a wall, the same architectural feature as a niche.

clue.text: Makes again word puzzle inspiring beginners to infer latest discovery

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: a rebus is a puzzle using pictures or symbols for words

indicators.note: beginners are those at the start, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A word puzzle that encourages newcomers to deduce the most recent find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' reads as motivating; in its breathing-in sense it signals that the initials go inside REBUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuild something is to construct it once more after it was damaged, which is making it a second time.

clue.text: Fight with European in predicament

parts.note: a scrap is an informal word for a brawl
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A brawl with a foreigner that leaves someone in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a container signal, but it is the link word; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting into a scrape means landing in an awkward or troublesome situation, so it is a synonym for a fix or jam.

clue.text: Some deplore bellicose figure not toeing the line?

indicators.note: some of something is only a part, so the letters come from within the words

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: People condemning a warlike person who refuses to obey orders.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'deploRE BELlicose'; the question mark flags the definition as a descriptive phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe the line is to conform, so a person who defies authority and will not conform is a dissident or insurgent.

clue.text: Place where drivers begin proceedings?

parts.note: surface reading: a starting grid or a courtroom where motorists face a case
setter's reading: drivers are the long clubs used to hit the ball off the tee at the start of each hole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests motorists and 'proceedings' suggests a court case; in fact the drivers are clubs that open play on each hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The driver is the club players use for the opening shot from the tee, and those tees are on the links where the game is played.

clue.text: Something that could be put across harbour in period of prosperity

definitions.text: Something that could be put across harbour
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a floating barrier stretched across a harbour mouth
second meaning: a time of rapid economic growth

explanation.surface: A barrier stretched across a port during good economic times.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a description rather than a synonym: a floating barrier is laid across a harbour to block ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a floating log or chain barrier across water and a sudden surge in trade and wealth.

clue.text: René sadly trapped by second journalist had a contemptuous look

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one piece sits within another
done sadly means gone wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, accent dropped, as anagram material
S is the abbreviation for second
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Poor René, cornered by another reporter, gave a disdainful look.
explanation.walkthrough: The name René is only letters; 'second' is the time abbreviation and journalist the standard ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneer is to curl the lip and smile scornfully, so the past tense matches showing disdain with one's face.

clue.text: Awkward opening to show given a slant

indicators.note: an opening is where something begins, so only its first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
tilted means set at an angle

explanation.surface: A clumsy first night of a show that was reviewed with a bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward opening' reads as one phrase about a bad premiere; 'Awkward' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech or writing is stiff and unnatural, lacking ease, which is an unpolished, clumsy quality.
